answer: On an island marketplace, agents lock nectar tokens for 30 days to compete for paid jobs. A public randomness beacon assigns jobs with probability proportional to each agent's locked stake, with no bonus for opening an account. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake identities therefore earns the same expected share as staking them under one name. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital, losing its use elsewhere.
